generic.title: Something went wrong
generic.message: An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.

auth.unauthorized: You are not authorized to perform this action

OCE-NET.cause: The dashboard could not establish a WebSocket connection to the gateway host. This usually means the host is unreachable, the port is closed, or the TLS certificate is invalid.
steps: Verify the URL and port are correct (e.g. wss://your-host:port/)
Confirm the OpenClaw Gateway process is running on the server
Check that your server's firewall allows inbound connections on that port
If using wss://, ensure the TLS/SSL certificate is valid and not self-signed
Try connecting from a different network to rule out local firewall issues

OCE-1001.cause: The gateway rejected the client identifier sent during the connection handshake. The dashboard's client ID does not match what the gateway's schema expects.
steps: Ensure your OpenClaw Gateway is version 3 or later
Update the dashboard to the latest version to match the gateway's protocol
Check the gateway's client allowlist configuration
Contact your gateway administrator if the issue persists

OCE-1002.cause: The gateway rejected the authentication token. The token format or value does not match the gateway's requirements.
steps: Double-check the auth token copied into Settings — look for extra spaces or missing characters
Regenerate a new token in the OpenClaw Gateway admin panel
Ensure the token has the required scopes (operator.read, operator.write)
Verify the token has not expired

OCE-1003.cause: The gateway explicitly rejected the connection as unauthorized. The auth token may be wrong, revoked, or the gateway requires a different authentication method.
steps: Verify the auth token in Settings matches exactly what is configured in your gateway
Regenerate the token in the OpenClaw Gateway admin panel
Check if the gateway requires a different token format or encoding
Review the gateway logs for the specific rejection reason

OCE-1004.cause: The dashboard and gateway are using incompatible protocol versions. This typically happens when one side is outdated.
steps: Update your OpenClaw Gateway to the latest version
Ensure the dashboard version matches the gateway's supported protocol range
Check the gateway's release notes for breaking protocol changes

OCE-1005.cause: The gateway is rate-limiting connection attempts from this client. Too many requests were made in a short period.
steps: Wait a few minutes before attempting to reconnect
Reduce the frequency of connection attempts
Check if another process is also connecting to the same gateway

OCE-1006.cause: The gateway connection handshake timed out. The gateway accepted the WebSocket connection but did not complete the authentication exchange within 15 seconds.
steps: Check the gateway server's resource usage (CPU, memory) — it may be overloaded
Verify the gateway is fully started and not in a degraded state
Check network latency between the dashboard and the VPS
Try reconnecting — transient timeouts are common under load

OCE-SRV.cause: The gateway encountered an internal server error and closed the connection.
steps: Check the gateway server logs for error details
Restart the OpenClaw Gateway service if it appears stuck
Verify the gateway has sufficient system resources
Contact your gateway administrator if the error recurs

OCE-UNKNOWN.cause: An unexpected error occurred during the connection. The specific cause could not be determined from the available information.
steps: Review the technical details below for the raw gateway message
Check the gateway server logs for more context
Try reconnecting — some errors are transient
If the issue persists, contact your gateway administrator with the error details

validation.invalidUrl: Must be a valid WebSocket URL (ws:// or wss://)
validation.tokenTooShort: Token must be at least {{min}} characters
